h1:
Samut Prakan for Nature Lovers
Bang Pu Seagulls + Cycling in Bang Krachao
intro: Samut Prakan sits right next to Bangkok, but drive out just a little and you can find both the sea and the forest in one trip. On day one you head to Bang Pu to feed the seagulls, walk the breezy Suk Ta Bridge and wait for the sunset. On day two you cross over to Bang Krachao, rent a bike and pedal past orchards and canals to fill your lungs with fresh air. This is a 2-day, 1-night plan with the timing already worked out, so there's no need to rush.

blocks.html: If you want to escape the city without driving far, Samut Prakan is the answer a lot of people overlook. On the eastern side is the Bang Pu seaside resort, a stretch of the Gulf of Thailand where migratory seagulls turn up every winter. On the western side is Bang Krachao, a pork-belly-shaped pocket of green that the Chao Phraya River loops almost all the way around — people call it the green lung of Bangkok. The two spots have completely different vibes but pair up nicely, so we put them together into a 2-day nature trip.

This trip works well if you drive yourself, or you can use public transport with a bit of extra planning around timing. The main thing to check first is the seagull season at Bang Pu, which runs from November to April. Come outside that window and you can still walk the bridge and look out over the sea, but you won't see the full flocks of birds.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Bang Pu: birds, mangrove walk and sunset

blocks.html: Day one is all about Bang Pu. There's no need to rush out at dawn, because the real highlights are from late afternoon into the evening, when the light goes soft and the birds come out to feed. Entry is free for both people and cars, and parking is easy.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Bang Pu — sea, birds and sunset

items.activity: Leave Bangkok heading for Bang Pu (km 37 on the old Sukhumvit Road)
items.note: Around 45 minutes to an hour from the city center, depending on traffic. If you're on public transport, bus 25 or 511 stops right at Bang Pu.

items.activity: Explore around the seaside resort, find parking, and stroll along the shore first
items.note: The sun is still strong at this hour, so look for photo angles and soak up the atmosphere for now.

items.activity: Lunch at Sala Suk Jai, at the end of Suk Ta Bridge
items.note: A seafood restaurant out over the water with a sea breeze. Order fresh seafood; expect around 200–400 THB per person. It gets busy on weekends, so arrive before early afternoon to snag a table with a good view.

items.activity: Walk the Army Nature Education Center (Bang Pu) and see the mangroves
items.note: A boardwalk runs through the mangrove forest. Free entry, open 9:00–16:00, with a bird hide and signs explaining the ecosystem.

items.activity: Head back to Suk Ta Bridge and buy chicken-fat scraps to feed the seagulls
items.note: Bags of chicken scraps are sold right at the head of the bridge for about 20–30 THB each. The birds swoop down to grab them — watch your valuables and hold onto your hat.

items.activity: Wait for the sunset at the end of the bridge
items.note: The light is best from about 16:00–18:00, with a cool breeze coming in. It's the favorite spot for photos with the flock of birds.

items.activity: Check in to your hotel in Samut Prakan town or the Pak Nam area
items.note: The Pak Nam zone has hotels at various price levels and is convenient for getting around the next day.

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.html: The seagulls are at their densest from November to April. If you come during the rainy season or late summer, the numbers drop off a lot — but Suk Ta Bridge and Sala Suk Jai are still open for a sea walk and a meal as usual.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Bang Krachao: rent a bike and breathe

blocks.html: Day two you cross over to Bang Krachao, in Phra Pradaeng district. Driving from Pak Nam takes about 30–40 minutes, or you can take the cross-river ferry from the Khlong Toei / Bang Na piers for a different feel. The area is known for cycling along orchards and narrow concrete paths that run beside the canals, shaded the whole way.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Bang Krachao — cycling, floating market, cafes

items.activity: Cross over to Bang Krachao and rent a bike near Sri Nakhon Khuean Khan Park
items.note: The rental shops are by the park entrance and near the temple. Prices are around 40 THB/hour, or 90–100 THB for the whole day.

items.activity: Cycle into Sri Nakhon Khuean Khan Park, over 200 rai of forest park
items.note: Free entry, open 6:00–19:00, with cycling routes throughout the park, a bird hide, a wooden bridge and a fish-feeding spot. The air is pleasantly cool in the morning.

items.activity: Cycle on to the 80th Anniversary Park at Khung Bang Krachao
items.note: A patch of green by the Chao Phraya with river viewpoints and nice photo spots — a good place to pause along the way.

items.activity: Stop at a cafe in the forest and rest with a coffee out of the sun
items.note: Bang Krachao has several cafes set among the trees, like Hiddenwoods, where you can sit in a glass-walled room or out by the river.

items.activity: If it's a Saturday or Sunday, head to Bang Nam Phueng Floating Market
items.note: Open Sat–Sun only, 8:00–16:00, with local food, the Mon community's canalside way of life, and handmade souvenirs.

items.activity: Cycle back, return the bike, and head back to Bangkok
items.note: Allow a little extra time if it's a busy weekend. Return the bike at the same shop you rented from.

blocks.title: About the bikes
blocks.html: Many stretches in Bang Krachao are narrow, raised concrete paths beside the canals, with no railing on the edge. Ride slowly, take care when passing others, and check the brakes and tires before leaving the shop every time. Wearing shoes you can pedal comfortably in is safer.

items: Timing — To see the birds in full, come to Bang Pu from November to April. Bang Krachao is cyclable year-round; morning or evening is more comfortable than midday.
Main costs — Bang Pu is free to enter; chicken scraps are 20–30 THB a bag. In Bang Krachao, bike rental is 90–100 THB for the whole day, and both parks are free to enter.

Getting around — Driving yourself is easiest since the two spots are on opposite sides of the province. Without a car, you can take the bus to Bang Pu, while for Bang Krachao most people take the cross-river ferry and then rent a bike.
What to bring — A hat, sunscreen, drinking water and mosquito repellent for the mangrove and park walks.
Floating market — Bang Nam Phueng Floating Market is open Saturdays and Sundays only. If you come on a weekday, skip it and focus on cycling the park instead.

blocks.text: Adapt the plan to suit you

items.name: Only one day
items.blurb: Pick one or the other. Want a chilled seaside afternoon watching birds? Go to Bang Pu from afternoon into the evening. Want exercise and fresh air? Go to Bang Krachao in the morning.

items.name: With kids
items.blurb: Feeding the birds at Bang Pu is fun for kids. In Bang Krachao, stick to cycling inside the park where the paths are wide and cars don't pass — it's safer.

items.name: For photographers
items.blurb: Line up the sunset at Suk Ta Bridge on day one, then on day two capture the forest cafes and the river views at the 80th Anniversary Park.

faq.q: When can you see the seagulls at Bang Pu?
faq.a: The seagulls migrate to Bang Pu from roughly November to April each year. The densest flocks and the best light come from late afternoon into the evening, around 16:00–18:00. Outside the season you can still walk Suk Ta Bridge and eat at Sala Suk Jai, but you won't catch the full flock.

faq.q: Is there an entry fee for Bang Pu?
faq.a: The Bang Pu seaside resort is free to enter for both people and cars, and parking is free too. The only costs are bags of chicken scraps for feeding the birds at 20–30 THB each, plus food if you eat at Sala Suk Jai.

faq.q: How much does it cost to rent a bike in Bang Krachao?
faq.a: The bike rental shops are near the entrance to Sri Nakhon Khuean Khan Park and around the temple. Prices are about 40 THB per hour, or 90–100 THB for the whole day. It's worth checking the brakes and tires before leaving the shop every time, since the canalside paths are fairly narrow.

faq.q: Are Bang Pu and Bang Krachao close together — can you do both in one day?
faq.a: The two spots are on opposite sides of the province. Bang Pu is to the east on the Gulf of Thailand, while Bang Krachao is to the west in Phra Pradaeng district. Driving between them takes about 40 minutes to an hour. You can do both in one day, but it's pretty rushed — splitting it into two days is more relaxed.

faq.q: What days is Bang Nam Phueng Floating Market open?
faq.a: Bang Nam Phueng Floating Market is open Saturdays and Sundays only, 8:00–16:00. If you visit Bang Krachao on a weekday the market is closed, so focus on cycling the parks and stopping at a cafe instead.
